candidate: sandbox-exec with an explicit deny-default profile and canonical path filters

observations.result: A custom deny-default profile allowed a canonical scratch root and allowed fixture, denied an outside read, denied an outside write, and denied a symlink from the allowed root to the outside root.
A profile allowing only /bin/bash denied /usr/bin/true and /bin/launchctl execution from the child.

A deny-default profile running /usr/bin/curl produced exit 6 with zero output for https://example.com; the built-in no-network profile also produced no DNS result. An allowlisted-network profile was not established.
MOP_CONTROLLER_SECRET set by the parent was printed by the sandboxed child. The sandbox does not clear inherited environment variables.

The sandbox-exec wrapper did not expose the test descriptor. Separately, the Broker ProcessSupervisor uses explicit stdio and a temporary parent file-descriptor canary test confirms that a non-stdio canary is not visible in the child.

artifact.test: process supervisor does not leak a parent file-descriptor canary

observations.limitation: This proves the current Broker launch boundary on the tested host, not every future executor or OS sandbox profile; it is not credential isolation proof.

observations.result: A sandboxed bash parent started /bin/sleep; terminating the parent left the child alive until the harness explicitly killed it. No Broker-owned process-group lease or descendant cleanup exists yet.
Fake SSH, cloud, Docker, and Keychain canary files outside the allowed root were denied by the profile. No real credential surface was opened or collected.
Keychain, SSH/cloud/package credential canaries, Docker authority, launchd persistence, privilege escalation, native binaries, scripts, and grandchildren require a dedicated hostile fixture.

decision: Do not select or enable sandbox-exec as the production task boundary. Keep mac_task_run disabled until a stronger, reproducible boundary proves credential, process-tree, network, persistence, and cleanup guarantees.
limitations: The fixture hashes above identify the non-secret test labels only; no user credential or private data was collected.
sandbox-exec is deprecated and profile semantics are platform-private; a passing profile is not a product guarantee.
No production task handler, signed app sandbox entitlement, VM/container boundary, or real external network allowlist is selected by this record.
